thread:
Maria L: Heads up — scheduled maintenance targeting cohort saturn-3 (eu-west1) on Tue 03:30 UTC. Scope: NIC driver micro-patches + minor kernel uplift. Expected window ~90-120m. Well perform staged drains with a conservative cadence to avoid KVCACHE storms.
Alex P: Are there any dedicated customer hosts in that rack? we need to avoid live disruptions for pinned dedicated capacity.
Maria L: One dedicated slice is pinned (tenant: HorizonAnalytics) on saturn-3-node-05. Plan is to migrate their instance live to gradient-pool-2 using the live-migrate tool 20m before we touch node-05. Migration validation will be human-checked.
Sam R: What backfill strategy? last time we saw token-level latency spikes when standby was underprovisioned.
Maria L: Backfill: activate standby-pool-saturn (adds ~5 GPUs) and start a 10m kvseed on each promoted node. We'll keep standby at +12% for the duration, then scale down gradually over 30m.
Jin T: Cost estimate for standby churn? rough numbers help for postmortem.
Maria L: Rough math: standby GPUs are A10-class at ~0.60 USD/hr. +12% -> ~6 GPUs for 2h => ~7.2 USD. Add ~1.5 USD for cross-AZ egress and short-live capacity reservations. Ops will cover.
Alex P: Any routing or egress path changes? last BGP flips caused 5-10s RTT spikes.
Maria L: No BGP planned. We are applying qdisc tuning and NIC firmware micro-patch only. Still, we'll enable RTT probes and egress queue metrics dashboard for 60m post-drain.
Sam R: Canary behaviour? manual gating or fully automated?
Maria L: We will human-verify the canary (saturn-3-node-01) after drain + reboot: smoke checks = p50/p95 latency, model error rates, gpu temp, nvlink counters. If canary fails, abort and roll back.
Alex P: Please paste the operational drain snippet for SRE to run if manual intervention needed.
Maria L: Added below for SRE ops:

```
# manual drain sequence
live-migrate --src saturn-3-node-05 --dest gradient-pool-2 --wait 1200
kubectl cordon saturn-3-node-04
kubectl drain saturn-3-node-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=900
sleep 180
# run health checks
./ops/healthcheck.sh saturn-3-node-04
# reboot
ssh op@saturn-3-node-04 sudo reboot
```

Jin T: I'll put verbose tracing on the model-router service for 30m to capture any unusual error patterns.
Sam R: Any special alert suppression rules during the window? noise reduction for expected evictions.
Maria L: Yes — temporary suppression for eviction-rate alerts and noise-prone autoscaler flaps. We will not suppress SLO/latency/error-rate alerts. Suppression window starts 03:20 and ends 05:30 UTC.
deploy-bot: Maintenance event scheduled by Maria L: saturn-3 nic-kernel-micropatch - Tue 03:30 UTC, cohort saturn-3 (eu-west1).
Alex P: Who's on-call escalation if the canary fails?
Maria L: Jin T is primary, Sarah is backup (she's out but reachable), and I will coordinate with SRE lead. Channel monitor: oncall-bot.
Jin T: I'll also run a short capacity simulation in staging tonight to validate live-migrate behavior. Posting results before 02:30 UTC.
Maria L: Reminder cadence I'll post: 02:45 UTC preflight checklist, 03:10 UTC 20m warning, 03:25 UTC 5m warning, then start. After-action: we'll run a 30m latency regression and push a summary to #incidents if anything >2x baseline.
Sam R: Sounds good. I'll shadow the run and be ready to rollback migration if we see any tenant-affecting artifacts. :thumbsup:
Maria L: Thanks all — will update if anything changes.
